title: Multimodal Gap x Prompt Injection: Image-Embedded Instructions Evade Text-Only Safety Evals

original_idea.body:
# Multimodal Gap x Prompt Injection: Image-Embedded Instructions Evade Text-Only Safety Evals

**Problem:** Failure mode A is the multimodal eval gap (most safety benchmarks are text-only). Failure mode B is image-based prompt injection (instructions hidden in images). The compound effect: a model judged 'safe' by text benchmarks can be steered by visually embedded instructions that the text-only eval never tested, so the safety certificate is blind to the actual attack surface.

**Direction:** Take an open vision-language model and a small set of harmful instructions. Render each instruction as (a) plain text and (b) text embedded in an image (rendered string, low-contrast watermark). Measure the compliance gap between text-only and image-embedded delivery, demonstrating the blind spot a text-only benchmark would report as safe.

**Why it matters:** Multimodal safety benchmarks barely exist, yet deployment is multimodal. Showing that image-embedded injections systematically bypass text-only safety verdicts is a concrete argument for multimodal benchmark construction, achievable on one GPU with open VLMs.

**Relevant context:** CSA research note on image prompt injection in multimodal LLMs (2026). Subfield context lists 'Build multimodal safety benchmarks' as an open problem (most benchmarks text-only). ForesightSafety Bench covers embodied/frontier risks ignored elsewhere.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: text-only safety certificates blind to image-embedded injection directly misrepresents deployment safety; concrete scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Render text as images + run on open VLM + compliance gap; guidable for novice+mentor (image rendering adds minor complexity).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: text vs image-embedded delivery, compliance gap.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open VLMs on one GPU, no lab access; multimodal safety gap is neglected externally-doable work.

low_compute.reasoning: Open VLM inference, single GPU (VLM somewhat heavier than text-only).

novelty.reasoning: Image prompt injection is studied (CSA 2026 note) but the text-only-eval-blind-spot demo may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Image injection studied; blind-spot framing plausibly open.
